Dear AC/SPC, the contribution combines strong sign-based optimization with a controlled comparison of 3 sign placements and their EF variants. At the same one-bit IID CNN2 budget, SignMuon achieves 85.72% versus SignSGD 81.44% (5 seeds), near Muon’s 85.98%. Centralized accuracy is 94.60% versus SignSGD 93.37% (3 seeds); nanoGPT loss is 3.2881 versus 3.4049 (one run/method). We credit prior/concurrent SignMuon and the general EF21 framework.

For Ueq5 and pqje (Q2), the submitted five-seed logs reproduce A8: MuonSign 82.94±0.19% versus SignSGD 81.44±0.15%. We will synchronize the main table and reverse that comparison. This correction uses submitted runs.

For Tx34 (Q1–2), our new proofs establish placement-specific ascent and smooth lower-bounded output-EF divergence. Theorem 4 excludes universal fixed-step rules, not decreasing schedules or horizon-tuned finite-time rates. The added conditional SignMuon theorem permits interacting layers under a uniform alignment margin; the EF21 refinements retain separability. The margin is unmeasured in our networks, and nanoGPT tests centralized updates after full-precision averaging. New Dirichlet(0.1) transfer at IID rates gives EF21-MuonSign 83.23±0.36% versus SignMuon 35.92±8.49% (5 seeds); retuning is pending. We ask that the strong sign-based results and precise theoretical contribution be weighed together.
